title: Picou's money, tile work and women
summary: Joe says Picou made his money from property and mosaic tile-setting, and got drinks and money from admirers.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Picou was a big drinker, too, wasn't he?
Oh, God. He had a lot of money at one time. A lot of money.
Did he own that barroom when you went to New Orleans and met him, or was that in later years?
When I first met him and went to take lessons from him when I was a kid, he didn't have any of that stuff. He didn't own any bar then.
It was on Robertson and Ursuline or somewhere like that.
He had two bars in New Orleans at one time. I know one was in Carlton(?).
Well, why did Picou amass all this money, and nobody else seemed to be... What made him so...
Oh, not his clarinet playing, then.
No. Picou was a tile-setter. He'd set tile. He was an artist. A lot of people don't know that.
No, I didn't. I knew he had a trade, but I couldn't remember what.
His daughter... I can't think of his daughter's name. Anyway, he came to Los Angeles and built a

garden, an outside garden where his daughter would... Inlaid mosaic tile all around in there, the most beautiful thing you've ever seen in your life. And that's why he made his money. And Picou didn't actually ever have to spend a lot of money for liquor. It was always given to him, you see. Or (?) bought him drinks and things like that. And he always had a lot of broads who would give him money.
